bandReport.notes: Page 18 opens cleanly at item 84 (its number, full stem and all six numbered statements are on the page); it does NOT open mid-item, so nothing is owed to the band that owns page 17. The band ends at item 100, the last item of the paper. All 17 items are whole and every one has exactly four printed options. Column crops: all eight were legible and none was sliced. p18 has the narrowest gutter in the booklet (22px at x=786) and its c1 crop carries a thin sliver of the RIGHT column's item numbers (86, 87, 88) down the far right margin - that is expected overlap, not a slice, and no right-column body text bled into c1. p19-c1, p19-c2, p20-c1 and p21-c1/c2 likewise carry only line-END letter slivers of the neighbouring column. p20-c2 clips the leading digit of item 96's number, rendering it as '06.'; the number is confirmed as 96 against p20.png, and no body text is lost. Both sparse right columns (p20-c2, p21-c2) were inspected individually and split correctly. No printed defect found: no duplicated option text, no item missing a fourth option, no garbled stem. Two wordings are transcribed verbatim and are as printed, not transcription slips: item 93 statement 1 reads 'measured up to a depth of 26 degree C isotherm which is 129 meters', and item 95 asks 'which of the following statements are correct ?' (plural 'are') where its neighbours use 'is/are'. Item 84 is the only item in the band with a six-entry statement list. Degree symbols (items 93, 99) and the CO2 subscript (item 85) are written as LaTeX; item 97's Famous Place / Present State pair list is written as a GitHub pipe table with its separator row.
